_comment: ADR 0047 §Wave 3.1 regression fixtures. Synthetic transcripts (no real user data) designed to expose over-consolidation patterns the cleaner_punctuation LLM pass historically exhibited under the old global SYSTEM_HEADER (Be concise...). With the per-pass preservation header shipped in Wave 1.1 (commit d6974a2), each fixture's expected_preserve phrases MUST survive byte-for-byte; the pass is whitespace + punctuation only. Each expected_preserve entry is matched against the LLM output as a whole-word phrase (lowercase, punctuation-stripped, whitespace-collapsed) — see runner.

fixtures.input: yesterday I was thinking about how the meeting last week went
I kind of feel like maybe we should rewrite the parser sort of from scratch
the dictionary entries which by the way are loaded from sqlite need to be capped at two hundred tokens
we should ship the dial feature even though the UI is not ready although the backend handles all four levels correctly
the model is qwen two point five three B I mean seven B for casual now
so basically what I want to say is the cleanup pipeline needs to stop dropping the preamble content I keep losing my first sentence every single time

fixtures._note: Originally included `q five toggle` in expected_preserve, but the prompt body explicitly ALLOWS numeral standardization (`q five` -> `Q5`). Replaced with a non-numeric preamble phrase so the fixture exercises content-preservation, not a behavior the prompt promises to do.
fixtures.input: okay let's plan the next sprint we have three big items the dial UI the mode eval rerun and the quant toggle and probably the documentation pass at the end
the length ratio shrink fallback fires whenever the cleaned text is less than sixty five percent of the input which is honestly a reasoned guess not a measured optimum
I was wondering whether we should hide the q five option entirely on machines with less than six gigabytes of vram or just default it off and let advanced users flip it
yesterday I dictated a really long meeting recap and the cleaner ate the second half because it decided the rest was redundant which obviously is not what I wanted
before I forget the migration that bumps the temperature also needs to be re evaluated against the baseline fixtures because the empirical justification only covered casual originally
the three modes we ship are casual which is the chatty one normal which is the default and formal which is for emails and documents
I guess if I had to pick one I would probably go with the length ratio guard since it's the cheapest defense and it catches the worst case directly
what's the actual user visible signal that the epic worked it's the edit free send column which flips true if the user doesn't tweak the output within five minutes
the vram probe runs at first boot and stores the result so we don't repeatedly query the gpu which is surprisingly expensive on some driver versions
originally I was going to flip the default cleanup level to light but actually we agreed to observe edit free send rates first before committing to that change
the most important thing honestly is that the cleaner punctuation pass never drops a single content word it has literally one job which is whitespace and punctuation
I want to add a feature where users can rerun the LLM pass on a saved dictation with a different prompt sort of like a transform menu
okay the deterministic preprocessor handles most cases fine but for the multi paragraph dictations we still need an LLM pass otherwise the structure is totally lost

so the way the new pipeline works is the preprocessor runs first then if the utterance is over twelve words and not listy we call the LLM and if the result is less than sixty five percent of the input we fall back to the preprocessor only output which is how we avoid the dropped preamble problem entirely
